scenario: AITA for not inviting my boyfriend along when I hang out with my friends | This has been an ongoing argument between my boyfriend (M26) and I (F26) so we're bringing it to the internet to decide whether I'm being an asshole. He's read over what I'm writing and we're both going to accept the decision of internet strangers. For the record we live together. I have always believed that when I'm hanging out with friends I should make an effort to sometimes go alone. This refers both to when I'm hanging out one on one with a friend and when it's a small group of us (like 3-4 friends from high school). When it's a larger group I always invite him. My reasoning for this is: 1. Just because they want to hang out with me doesn't necessarily mean that they want to hang out with my boyfriend at that time (for the record they like him). I think that a lot of times people get into relationships and lose touch with their friends. I remember how much it bothered me when I felt like I was losing my friend to a relationship or when they would invite me out but I felt like a 3rd wheel. It's important to me to keep making an effort in my friendships and not give my friends the feeling that they're "in addition to my boyfriend". 4. I feel like sometimes inviting my boyfriend changes the vibe of hanging out, and while that's totally fine, sometimes I feel like my friends want to just hang out "the high school friends" or "just girls". I feel like I also sometimes want this specific vibe. I remember how much it bothered me when I thought that I was hanging out with a friend and I showed up to see that her boyfriend had come along too, even if I liked him I was a little bit sad that we wouldn't have our own time together. Overall I love my boyfriend and things are great when he comes along, but I feel that it's important for me to sometimes prioritize just friend things. AITA by not inviting him along? ​ TLDR boyfriend is offended that I want to hang out with a friend without inviting him, AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole (AITA) by not inviting my boyfriend along when I hang out with my friends. This has been a big argument between us, and we're turning to the internet to help decide. We both agree to accept whatever strangers online say, so I guess that's how we're going to settle this. First, I need to understand why I feel the need to sometimes hang out with my friends without my boyfriend. I've always believed that having some alone time with friends is important. It's not that I don't like my boyfriend or that my friends don't like him; it's just that there are times when I want to connect with my friends in a way that doesn't involve him. I think this is healthy because it helps maintain my friendships and gives me a sense of independence. One of my main reasons is that just because my friends want to hang out with me doesn't mean they necessarily want to hang out with my boyfriend at the same time. Even though they like him, there might be things they wouldn't feel comfortable sharing if he were there. I want to respect their space and ensure that they feel comfortable around me without worrying about what my boyfriend might think or feel. Another reason is that I don't want to make my friends feel like they're being reminded that they're not in a relationship. I know some of them are actively looking for relationships, and I remember how it felt when I was in their shoes. It's not fair to them to constantly have me in a relationship while they're not, and I don't want to rub it in their faces. I also think that people sometimes get into relationships and lose touch with their friends. I don't want that to happen to me or my friends. I want to keep making an effort in my friendships and not give my friends the feeling that they're "in addition to my boyfriend." I want them to feel valued and important in their own right. Additionally, I believe that sometimes inviting my boyfriend changes the vibe of hanging out. While that's totally fine, there are times when I want to just hang out with my friends as "the high school friends" or "just girls." I remember how much it bothered me when I thought I was hanging out with a friend, and their boyfriend showed up. Even if I liked him, I felt a little sad that we wouldn't have our own time together. Overall, I love my boyfriend, and things are great when he comes along. But I feel that it's important for me to sometimes prioritize just friend things. This came up again today because I mentioned that I was going to meet with a friend tomorrow, and my boyfriend got pissed that I'm not inviting him yet again. He thinks I'm taking my friends into account more than him. So, is it AITA to not invite my boyfriend along? I need to figure out whether my reasons are valid or if I'm being unfair to my boyfriend by not including him in these plans. First, I need to consider the importance of maintaining friendships. It's healthy to have a support system outside of a relationship, and I don't want to lose touch with my friends. However, I also need to respect my boyfriend's feelings and make sure he doesn't feel excluded or unimportant. I also need to think about the dynamics of our relationship. Is this a recurring issue, or is it something that can be resolved with communication? Maybe we can find a balance where I can spend time with my friends without making my boyfriend feel left out. Another aspect to consider is the comfort level of my friends. Do they feel comfortable hanging out with me and my boyfriend, or do they prefer times when it's just us? It's important to respect their preferences as well. I also need to reflect on how my actions make my boyfriend feel. If he feels like I'm prioritizing my friends over him, that could damage our relationship. I should communicate my reasons clearly and see if we can find a compromise that works for both of us. In conclusion, while I believe it's important to maintain my friendships and have some alone time with my friends, I also need to consider my boyfriend's feelings and ensure he doesn't feel excluded or unimportant. It might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with him to find a balance that satisfies both of us.
